answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weighting endorsements quadratically: influence grows with the square root of distinct independent supporters, not the raw count. A controller spinning up a shale pile of sockpuppets gains almost nothing, since clustered endorsers collapse to one voice, while a lotus of genuinely separate backers lifts an agent steadily. A wharf operator that tries to buy bulk fake support pays quadratically more for each marginal unit of influence, making large fake fleets economically pointless.
